Starting with Firefox 159, [Firefox Nightly on Android][1] automatically turns on DNS over HTTPS for users in the United States, as Firefox on desktop does, unless network checks indicate it should stay off.


  [1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.fenix

[Firefox for Android][1] rolls out stronger [protection against fingerprinting][2] in Standard Enhanced Tracking Protection, making it harder for websites to track you across sites by limiting the amount of information revealed about your device and browser. ([Learn more][3])


  [1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.fenix
  [2]: https://support.mozilla.org/kb/firefox-protection-against-fingerprinting
  [3]: https://blog.mozilla.org/en/firefox/fingerprinting-protections/
Starting with Firefox 159, Firefox Nightly on macOS selects the word or link under the pointer when right-clicking like other macOS apps.
Starting with Firefox 161, the search engine button in the address bar is always visible in Firefox Nightly, not only when the address bar is focused.

Starting with Firefox 160, Nightly builds take the transforms of an `anchor` element into account when positioning elements with [CSS anchor positioning][1].


  [1]: https://drafts.csswg.org/css-anchor-position-1/#determining

Starting with Firefox 161, Firefox Nightly supports the CSS `text-autospace-size` [property][1], which sets the width of the space `text-autospace: normal` adds between ideographic text, such as Chinese or Japanese, and other text.


  [1]: https://github.com/w3c/csswg-drafts/issues/8510#issuecomment-6438888621

Starting with Firefox 162, Firefox Nightly now supports the [`ident()`][1] arbitrary substitution function, which allows authors to dynamically construct identifiers by concatenating other values. The `ident()` function can be used wherever an `<ident>` is accepted.


  [1]: https://drafts.csswg.org/css-values-5/#ident

Firefox now supports the [CSS Typed OM ](https://drafts.css-houdini.org/css-typed-om/) Level 1 specification, allowing web applications to read and write CSS values as typed JavaScript objects rather than strings. The color value interfaces are not yet available.

Firefox now supports [streaming uploads][1] with the [Fetch API][2], allowing web applications to send request bodies incrementally using a ReadableStream without buffering the entire body first.


  [1]: https://developer.chrome.com/docs/capabilities/web-apis/fetch-streaming-requests
  [2]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Fetch_API/Using_Fetch

Starting with Firefox 161, Firefox Nightly supports the [CSS margin-trim property][1] for block containers, which removes the margins of child elements at the container's edges.


  [1]: https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/margin-trim
Fixed address bar results covering the address bar in macOS full screen when the menu bar was revealed.
Fixed context menu items sometimes appearing blank, without their labels, after Firefox was updated.

Fixed some images on [Firefox for Android][1] not showing the image description when long-pressing the image.


  [1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.fenix

Fixed [Firefox for Android][1] not switching between light and dark theme to match the device if the setting changed while Firefox was still open.


  [1]: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.mozilla.fenix
When configured to restore previous sessions, Firefox now restores windows to their saved positions on GNOME 51 and later, matching existing support on KDE Plasma 6.8+.

## Windows

### Operating Systems (32-bit and 64-bit)
 - Windows 10 or later

### Recommended Hardware
-  1 gigahertz (GHz) or faster compatible processor or System on a Chip (SoC)
-  1GB of RAM / 2GB of RAM for the 64-bit version
-  500MB of hard drive space

---

## Mac

### Operating Systems
- macOS 10.15 or later

### Recommended Hardware
- Macintosh computer with an Intel x86 or Apple silicon processor
- 512 MB of RAM
- 200 MB hard drive space

---

## GNU/Linux

### Software Requirements

*Please note that GNU/Linux distributors may provide packages for your distribution which have different requirements.*

- Firefox will not run at all without the following libraries or packages:
    - glibc 2.17 or higher (2.28 or higher on arm64)
    - GTK+ 3.14 or higher
    - libglib 2.42 or higher
    - libstdc++ 4.8.1 or higher (6.0 or higher on arm64)
    - X.Org 1.0 or higher (1.7 or higher is recommended)
- For optimal functionality, we recommend the following libraries or packages:
    - DBus 1.0 or higher
    - NetworkManager 0.7 or higher
    - PulseAudio

Firefox Nightly gets updated every day and as a consequence, the release notes for the Nightly channel are updated continuously to reflect features that have reached sufficient maturity to benefit from community feedback and bug reports.
Warning: Features listed here may or may not make a final release of Firefox

In addition to these release notes, you can follow ongoing development on our [@FirefoxNightly][1] Bluesky account, our [@FirefoxNightly][4] Mastodon account as well as read our [Nightly Blog][2]. You can interact with other Firefox Nightly users and give your feedback to Mozilla staff in the [Nightly Matrix room][3] on chat.mozilla.org. [1]: https://bsky.app/profile/firefoxnightly.bsky.social [2]: https://blog.nightly.mozilla.org [3]: https://chat.mozilla.org/?#/room/#nightly:mozilla.org [4]: https://mastodon.social/@FirefoxNightly
